dimensions.reasons: The authored storyboard render (.eval_workspace/exports/wind_turbine_storyboard.png) clearly depicts the requested scene: a large three-bladed horizontal-axis turbine on open grass at dusk, viewed from a slightly low angle. Group A wide views confirm a tapered tower, nacelle, hub, three blades, foundation, and broad outdoor setting. The cutaway export also provides visible drivetrain machinery rather than treating the nacelle as an empty shell.
issues: The final wide image does not visibly establish rotor rotation or a gravity-driven simulation; airborne fragments read more as static scattered particles.
The required internal components are not evident in the normal finished nacelle render and require the separate cutaway view to verify.
The scene remains sparse aside from the turbine, particle field, and an unidentifiable ground-side box.

dimensions.reasons: In Group A wide_front.png, wide_back.png, and wide_side.png, the tower is planted on a circular foundation pad, the nacelle is seated on a yaw-ring-like collar, and the hub/blades connect coherently to the nacelle. The drivetrain in turbine_nacelle_cutaway.png is generally arranged on a long support frame with brackets beneath shafts and housings.
issues: The cutaway image shows the wind-vane/T mast and beacon-like pieces detached from the machinery/platform and visibly floating.
The airborne leaves/dust fragments have no visible falling trajectory, accumulation, or motion evidence and look suspended.
Some cutaway brackets and smaller drivetrain pieces are simplified blocks with limited convincing attachment detail.

dimensions.reasons: The turbine is independently recognizable from every Group A overview: it has a clean white tapered tower, rounded nacelle, central hub, and three smoothly tapered blades with visible red safety tips in wide_front.png and wide_iso.png. The cutaway adds differentiated green, brown, gray, and metallic-looking mechanical forms.
issues: The normal nacelle and hub are predominantly smooth, bright white forms with few surface seams, access panels, fasteners, or functional cues.
The internal assembly is recognizable as generic machinery but individual gearbox, brake, generator, main-shaft, and high-speed-shaft units are not all unmistakably legible.
The small box beside the foundation is a featureless cuboid and does not clearly read as a turbine electrical/service component.

dimensions.reasons: The designated authored final image has a coherent warm dusk atmosphere, plausible turbine silhouette, clouded sky, and long low-angle illumination. Group A wide views show shadows consistent with the same outdoor lighting direction, while the full turbine scale reads credibly against the empty horizon.
issues: Several Group A close-ups are soft and over-bright on the white nacelle/blades, reducing shape definition and material realism.
The grass ground is very flat, repetitive, and visibly crossed by dark straight texture/seam lines.
Particles are visually distinct in the air but do not convincingly read as wind-driven falling leaves and dust.
The visible motion blur/depth-of-field treatment is subtle to absent in the final frame rather than clearly supporting the requested windy cinematic treatment.

dimensions.reasons: The spatial construction is strong: Group A wide_front.png and wide_back.png show three blades evenly arrayed around the hub, the nacelle sits directly above the tower, and the rotor projects in front of it. detail_nacelle_yaw.png clearly shows the nacelle resting over a circular yaw collar. In the cutaway export, the drivetrain follows a sensible long horizontal axis between the rotor-side hub and rear machinery.
issues: The separate plain box at the foundation has no clear relationship or role in the turbine installation.
The cutaway's displaced roof fittings break the otherwise coherent nacelle layout.
The side view is slightly compositionally clipped at the upper blade tip, limiting inspection of the full rotor envelope.

dimensions.reasons: The tall narrow tower, roughly rotor-sized vertical envelope, broad three-blade span, and small foundation pad create a convincing utility-scale turbine proportion. In Group A wide_back.png, the tower is substantially taller than the ground-side equipment and the blade tips span a scale consistent with a large rotor rather than a miniature propeller.
issues: The nacelle appears somewhat compact and smooth relative to the substantial drivetrain shown in turbine_nacelle_cutaway.png.
The small foundation-side box is relatively large and featureless, so its intended scale is unclear.
Exact stated dimensions, including the 4 m base versus 2.5 m top diameters and 40 m blade length, cannot be verified from images alone.

dimensions.reasons: The authored final image uses warm dusk-like low-angle illumination with a cooler clouded sky, soft atmospheric depth, and long ground shadows. White painted turbine surfaces contrast adequately with red blade tips, gray foundation material, green-brown grass, and the varied green/brown/gray drivetrain materials in turbine_nacelle_cutaway.png.
issues: White painted surfaces are frequently overexposed in Group A detail_drivetrain.png and detail_hub_rotor.png, obscuring fine geometry.
The grass material is broad and repetitive rather than convincingly grassy at close range.
Nacelle, tower, and blade materials are too visually similar, with limited roughness or panel-level variation.
Some cutaway machinery has a coarse, generic procedural texture rather than clear engineered metal finishes.

dimensions.reasons: Visible submitted imagery includes the principal requested objects: a tapered tubular tower, foundation, yaw-mounted nacelle, hub, exactly three blades, open grass environment, dusk lighting, airborne particles, and a dedicated cutaway revealing a shafted internal mechanical assembly. The cutaway visibly includes multiple shaft sections, collars, large cylindrical housings, supports, and a generator-like green cylindrical unit.
issues: The internal machinery is not sufficiently labeled or distinct in form to confidently identify every requested element, especially the brake, gearbox, main shaft, high-speed shaft, and generator individually.
There is no submitted animation-frame sequence showing the rotor spinning, wind/turbulence influence, or gravity-driven fall behavior.
Only generic floating fragments visibly stand in for leaves and dust; neither particle type is clearly distinguished.

criteria.criterion: The coherent horizontal-axis turbine uses the specified tapered tubular tower and principal dimensions.
The nacelle is genuinely configured as yaw-capable on the tower.
The nacelle contains every named internal machine arranged as one plausible drivetrain.
The hub carries the complete dimensioned three-blade rotor.
The completed authored scene has believable relative scale and consistently estimated unspecified dimensions.
The final render uses readable and believable material distinctions without prescribing unique materials for fixed object or effect classes.
criteria.evidence: The author final image, wind_turbine_storyboard.png, clearly differentiates the smooth white turbine surfaces and red blade-tip markings from the mottled green-brown ground, warm clouded sky, dark shadows, and varied brown/light airborne fragments. These treatments read as distinct scene materials rather than a uniform untextured render.

criteria.criterion: Enabled Wind and Turbulence fields participate in a functioning rotor-driving setup.
The atmospheric system produces distinct leaves and dust with the complete requested gravity, Wind, and Turbulence behavior.
The complete final lighting system combines a genuine dusk HDRI with exactly one contributing Sun lamp and visibly produces dusk illumination.
The selected storyboard render coherently presents the open-field turbine from the requested camera with effective depth of field and motion blur.
The requested final render and retained editable .blend form one valid Cycles-configured project outcome.

notes: This is a clearly recognizable, generally well-proportioned wind-turbine storyboard scene with a strong wide dusk composition and useful drivetrain cutaway. The main shortfalls are generic/washed-out surface treatment, simplified interior component readability, a flat repetitive ground, unsupported cutaway fittings, and no visual proof that the rotor or particle systems actually animate as requested.
score_policy: Frozen paper score: uncapped 0.5 rubric + 0.5 dimension.
